note: Normative rules no conformance case can demonstrate, and what stands in for one. A rule reaches this file only when a document cannot exercise it — because it is about a collection of documents, about the specification itself, or about a consumer's display. `evidence` names what does hold it: a repository check, a test file, or `gap` when nothing does. Read alongside conformance/coverage.json, which ratchets the rules cases do cover. Checked by `pnpm check rule-coverage`.

4.4.3.why: Supersession orders documents sharing an id, and the suite runs one document at a time — a case holding two would be a different suite. The reference implementation provides the operation instead, as `supersedes(a, b)`, and its tests cover both what the rule decides and what it declines to.

4.5.2.why: Addressed to producers choosing how to publish several languages. It forbids nothing a document can violate — §4.5.1 already covers prose without a declared language, and that has a case.

5.2.4.why: A SHOULD about the unit vocabulary. No diagnostic reports it, so it is enforced over this repository's own documents, where a unit outside the vocabulary for its kind fails the build.

5.2.5.why: A rendering rule. The conformance runner compares validity, diagnostics and derived rankings — never display — so the reference formatter's tests are what hold it.

5.2.7.why: A rendering rule, on the same terms as §5.2.5.

6.1.3.why: States what participant identity does not span. It defines a boundary rather than requiring anything of a document, so there is nothing for a case to accept or reject.

7.2.8.why: A duty on the producer: choose the most specific status true of an aggregate. Which status is true of an aggregate depends on the sport, so no validator can tell a correct choice from a lazy one. A case could show the recommended shape and would demonstrate nothing.

8.3.6.why: A display obligation, and the runner compares validity, diagnostics and derived rankings — never what is drawn. The viewer renders the admission document whose positions are its whole result, and the test checks the order shown is the published one rather than the declaration order.

10.2.3.why: Preservation is a property of a read-write cycle. The runner reads and never writes, so the round-trip tests are what hold it: unknown members, nested unknown members, x- extensions at every level, and unknown enumeration values kept verbatim despite being read as fallbacks.

11.2.2.why: Constrains what a future MINOR version may do. Nothing in this version can violate it; the first 1.1 draft is what it governs.

11.5.1.why: The producer profile. Every document in the corpus is one, and the check validates all of them with no error.

11.5.2.why: Defines the `reading` level the suite selects cases by. The levels are read out of the runner so the two cannot drift, and a case declaring a level the runner does not know fails rather than being skipped.

11.5.3.why: Defines the `ranking` level, on the same terms as §11.5.2.

11.5.4.why: Defines the `rewriting` level, on the same terms as §11.5.2.

11.6.1.why: Proposes a media type whose registration is pending. Nothing to run until a registry answers.

11.6.2.why: Requires a consumer to accept `application/json`. It governs an HTTP exchange and the suite reads documents from disk. No consumer here looks at the header — the proposed media type is unregistered and almost no server sends it, so discriminating on it would reject nearly every document published today. The tests serve one document under three media types so that adding such a check would have to be a decision rather than an oversight.

11.6.3.why: The recommended file extension. Every document under examples/ must be named *.openresult.json, which the check enforces rather than assuming.

12.1.1.why: The distinction between an error and a warning is what the suite is built on: an invalid case names errors, a valid case may name warnings, and a warning has never made a document invalid. Every case exercises it, which is why none cites it.

12.1.2.why: That a validator reports both, distinctly, on the same terms as §12.1.1: the report separates them and the runner compares them separately.

12.1.3.why: Every diagnostic must carry a location, the rule in plain language and at least one concrete correction. `diagnostic()` takes all three as required parameters, so a call that omits the correction does not build; `diagnostics-cite-rules` checks the signature has not grown an optional marker back. The first attempt at this read the call sites with a regular expression, passed, and had missed the one call it was written to find.

12.2.1.why: A published code is permanent. The check ratchets the code list: a code that has existed must go on existing, and removing one fails.

12.3.1.why: The rule this file exists to serve. The check is what reads it.
